summary: Streaming responses disconnect in TypeScript quickstart (SSE ends early / ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE)
description:
Customer report (PineconeAI): TypeScript quickstart streaming example frequently disconnects mid-response.

Issue summary
- Streaming SSE response terminates early; customer sees partial output and then an exception.
- Reproducible from their dev environment running the quickstart unmodified (Node 18).

Impact
- Blocks evaluation of streaming for the Hosted API.
- Customer perception: reliability issue; unclear whether they are doing something wrong.

Environment
- Customer runtime: Node v18.19.0, macOS + corporate network (proxy/VPN).
- Redwood: Hosted API, region us-east.
- Quickstart: redwood-quickstarts template (TS) using fetch + ReadableStream.

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Clone quickstart and set REDWOOD_API_KEY.
2) Run `npm install` then `npm run start`.
3) Invoke streaming sample 5-10 times.
4) Observe intermittent disconnect after ~20–90 seconds; typically after several SSE chunks.

Observed behavior
- The stream ends unexpectedly; customer receives an error similar to:
  - `TypeError: terminated` (undici)
  - `Error [ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE]: Premature close`
- When it fails, it fails without a clean final `[DONE]` or last event.

Expected behavior
- Streaming continues until model finishes and the server sends `[DONE]` (or equivalent completion signal).

Customer-provided logs
- Node console:
  2026-02-03T19:22:14.981Z info: starting stream request
  2026-02-03T19:23:07.412Z error: Error [ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE]: Premature close
  2026-02-03T19:23:07.413Z error: TypeError: terminated

Redwood-side investigation notes
- Found corresponding request IDs in gateway logs (examples below) where the client closed the connection before the server completed generation.
- Gateway log snippets:
  2026-02-03T19:23:07.401Z api-gateway sse_stream_end reason=client_disconnect status=499 request_id=req_01J0Q6H7J7S1A3G2P8GZ3J5T3N org_id=org_8w3... project_id=prj_2c1... route=/v1/chat/completions model=redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct stream=true bytes_sent=18422 duration_ms=52433

- Correlation: failures cluster when token throughput is low (longer-lived streams) and customer is on corporate proxy/VPN.
- Hypothesis: intermediate proxy closes idle/long-lived HTTP connections if no data for a period; our stream can have >30s gaps for some prompts.

Workaround provided to customer
1) Use the official Redwood TypeScript SDK streaming helper (handles stream reading + resilience) instead of the raw fetch example.
2) If staying on raw fetch: ensure the consumer continuously drains the ReadableStream; do not buffer the entire response before reading events.
3) Ask customer to test from a non-proxied network (hotspot) to validate proxy interference.

Resolution
- We updated:
  (a) TS SDK streaming to be more resilient to partial frame boundaries + read-loop termination edge cases.
  (b) Quickstart + docs with explicit troubleshooting guidance for streaming disconnects, including corporate proxy/VPN notes and recommended client patterns.

Docs link sent to customer
- Troubleshooting: Streaming disconnects (new section): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/troubleshooting/streaming-disconnects

Next steps (internal)
- Track whether we should add periodic SSE heartbeat comments for long gaps (requires product/infra signoff due to token/cost/metrics implications).
- Add a lightweight detection metric for abnormal 499 rates on streaming routes by org to proactively flag onboarding issues.

customer_facing_message: We found the disconnects were coming from the network path (corporate VPN/proxy) closing long-lived streaming connections, and the raw fetch-based quickstart was more sensitive to early termination. We recommend using the official Redwood TypeScript SDK streaming helper (updated for stability) and following the troubleshooting guidance here: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/troubleshooting/streaming-disconnects. The updated quickstart now uses the SDK pattern as well.
